title: Import and distribute
tagline: Buying abroad — China, Vietnam, Europe — and selling in India through distributors, marketplaces or your own brand.
who: Traders importing finished goods or components
Distributors for foreign brands in India

structure.why: Import consignments carry real liability (customs disputes, product safety, BIS, distributor contracts) and need bank credit (LCs, buyer’s credit) — lenders and foreign suppliers prefer a company. A proprietor can import legally, but limited liability matters when a container is held.
structure.alternatives: Proprietorship for small courier-mode imports to test products.

breakdown: BIS CRS (electronics) per model: ₹25,000–1.5 lakh incl. testing

timeline: Company + GST + IEC inside a month; BIS (if needed) 2–4 months; first container 6–10 weeks door to door.
taxes: Customs: Basic Customs Duty on CIF value (0–150% by ITC-HS; FTA rates with a certificate of origin) + 10% Social Welfare Surcharge on BCD + IGST on (CIF + BCD + SWS). IGST is input credit; BCD and SWS are cost.
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties on many Chinese goods (steel, chemicals, solar, tiles) — check CBIC before pricing.
GST on resale at the HSN rate; e-way bills for movements above ₹50,000.
TCS on foreign remittance for imports does not apply to business import payments through proper banking channels (Form A1).
selling: Distributors and dealers (sign agreements with territory and payment terms)
Marketplaces — importer name/address and country of origin must appear on labels and listings
Own brand D2C after BIS/label compliance
B2B platforms and GeM for government buyers
sourcing: Alibaba (Trade Assurance), 1688 via agents, Made-in-China, Global Sources; fairs: Canton Fair, Yiwu market, HK Electronics Fair
Verify suppliers: business licence, factory audit (SGS/QIMA/TÜV inspection ₹20,000–40,000 per visit), samples, 30/70 payment terms
Incoterms: start with FOB and your own freight forwarder; DDP hides duty surprises
pitfalls: Shipping electronics without the foreign factory’s BIS registration — customs will not release the goods.
Undervaluing invoices to save duty — Customs uses valuation databases; penalties plus confiscation.
Forgetting MRP/importer stickers before clearance under Legal Metrology — re-labelling in a bonded warehouse is slow and expensive.
Paying suppliers via personal remittances or crypto — import payments must go through your AD bank with the Bill of Entry matched (IDPMS).
Ignoring restricted/prohibited lists and licence needs (e.g., laptops/IT hardware under the import management system, certain chemicals, used goods).
